items.title: These Stocks Are Making Moves Today, Thanks to SpaceX
items.summary: SpaceX has designs to leverage its dominant position in the space business into a dominant position in AI and communications.  SpaceX stock, for starters, was down about 12% at $110.  Nvidia shares were up 3.1% partly because SpaceX is using their chips for its Starmind AI computing satellites.

items.title: Lumen Posts Narrower-Than-Expected Q2 Loss, Revenues Drop Y/Y
items.summary: LUMN's Q2 loss came in narrower than expected as strategic revenues have risen 14.1% and free cash flow has turned positive despite a 9.3% revenue decline.

items.title: Is AT&T (T) Cheap On SpaceX Mobile Competition Fears?
items.summary: AT&T (T) is back in focus after SpaceX outlined plans for a full mobile service that would combine Starlink satellites with ground infrastructure, sharpening competitive questions around long term wireless customer retention. See our latest analysis for AT&T. The AT&T share price has been choppy around competitive headlines, with a 1-day share price return that declined 0.89% and a 7-day move down 5.19%. items.title: Telecom shares decline as SpaceX outlines plans for mobile network expansion
items.summary: Shares of major U. S. wireless providers moved lower after SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) revealed plans to develop a fully integrated mobile service, raising concerns that Starlink could eventually become a direct competitor to Verizon (NYSE:VZ), AT&T (NYSE:T) and T-Mobile (NASDAQ:TMUS).

items.title: SpaceX plans terrestrial mobile network to rival AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile
items.summary: SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said the company intends to build out ground-based infrastructure to complement its satellite service

items.title: SpaceX’s Starlink Threat Sends T, VZ, TMUS Stocks Lower Premarket – But Telecom CEOs Have Said Satellite Isn’t A Real Concern Yet
items.summary: Despite the market reaction, executives at all three telecom companies recently said satellite broadband is unlikely to materially threaten their core businesses.

items.title: Telecom stocks fall after SpaceX signals push into mobile service
items.summary: Investing.com -- U.S. wireless stocks tumbled Tuesday after SpaceX signaled plans to build a full-fledged mobile service, raising the prospect that Starlink could eventually compete directly with Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile.

items.title: Telecom Stocks Slip After SpaceX Takes Aim at Their Market Share
items.summary: SpaceX is coming for large U.S. telecom providers. During the company’s first earnings call, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell referenced the revenue that AT&T, Verizon Communications and T-Mobile US pull in, and said Starlink would take aim at their subscribers.
